title: Customs Amendment (2017 Harmonized System Changes) Bill 2016
short_title: Customs Amendment (2017 Harmonized System Changes) Bill 2016

summary.attribution: Written by a model from the explanatory memorandum; not the record
sentences: The bill would update customs references for biofuels and biofuel blends to reflect revised international tariff classifications and imports covered by the China-Australia Free Trade Agreement.
It would replace two tariff subheadings in the biofuel blend definition and add references to the tariff schedule implementing the trade agreement’s import duty treatment.
The substantive changes would commence with the companion Customs Tariff Amendment legislation on 1 January 2017, as part of implementing the international Harmonized System review.
changes: The biofuel blend definition would refer to subheadings 3824.99.30 and 3824.99.40 instead of the superseded classifications.
The imported biofuel treatment provision would include Schedule 12 of the Customs Tariff Act.
The biofuel blend definition would also recognise that trade agreement schedule.
summary.affected: Importers of biofuels and biofuel blends covered by the amended customs provisions are affected.

speeches.speaker: Alex Hawke
speeches.brief: The bill amends the Customs Act 1901 to implement changes from the fifth review of the World Customs Organization's harmonized system and to collect import duties on biofuels and biofuel blends under the China-Australia Free Trade Agreement.

speeches.speaker: Alex Hawke
speeches.brief: The speaker summed up two bills implementing Australia's obligations from the World Customs Organization's fifth review of the Harmonized System, introducing about 150 amendments to the Customs Tariff Act 1995 and minor changes to the Customs Act 1901, including new tariff classifications for emerging technologies and provisions for collecting import duties on biofuels under the China-Australia Free Trade Agreement.
